SELL.md:
**The other side: selling the premium, with one rule to stand aside** (2008–2026; protocol 5, written before the run). Sell 1M S&P 500 variance at the VIX, one tranche a day, held to expiry. Switch: no new sale when, at the previous close, VIX3M/VIX was in the bottom 20% of its own past (544 days in 53 episodes, 12% of the time).

| Seller of 1M variance at the VIX | P&L per year (vol pts) | Max drawdown | P&L per year / max drawdown | Worst tranche | Time in market |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Every day | +21.2 | -173.8 | 0.12 | -252.2 | 100% |
| **With the switch** | +22.9 | -111.6 | 0.21 | -252.2 | 88% |

| Criterion fixed in advance | Result | Met? |
|---|---|---|
| Max drawdown at least one third smaller | -173.8 → -111.6 (-36%) | yes |
| P&L per year / max drawdown higher | 0.12 → 0.21 | yes |
| Seller's P&L per tranche lower on OFF days than on any day (time-shift test) | -1.19 vs +1.80, p = 0.051 | **no** |
| Still lower when any one OFF episode is left out | worst case +1.44 vs +1.80 | yes |

**Not retained**: the time-shift test gives p = 0.051, above the 5% bar fixed in advance. The miss is narrow (3 of 4 criteria met, and a p-value drawn from 2,000 random shifts is itself known to about ±0.005), but the rule was written before the run and it fails as written: a lead for the forward test, not a validated switch. Selling on OFF days lost money in 4 of 53 episodes (average per episode +4.8 vol pts per tranche; ON days average +2.20). The switch does not avoid the first hit: the worst tranche (-252 vol pts) was sold on a day the switch allowed, before the curve inverted; what it removes is the selling that follows. The sample starts in 2008-07, when the percentile first exists. The every-day seller's premium is the stable result of this page; it comes with the drawdown shown in the table, and VIX² is not an executable strike (no bid-offer, no costs).
